newsitem.title: USA: U.S. general's promotion delayed over Saudi blast.
newsitem.headline: U.S. general's promotion delayed over Saudi blast.

text.p: The U.S. Air Force said on Wednesday it had delayed the promotion of Brig. Gen. Terryl Schwalier to major general in a controversy over last year's bombing in Saudi Arabia that killed 19 U.S. troops.

Schwalier, who commanded U.S. air operations in Saudi Arabia when the truck bomb ripped a military housing complex in Dhahran on June 25, was already nominated by President Bill Clinton and confirmed by the Senate for the promotion.

He is scheduled to pin on his second general's star on Feb. 1, but the Air Force said in a brief announcement that it was delaying that authorisation "pending the resolution of an inquiry into the circumstances" of the blast.

A Pentagon report issued last year was scathing in putting responsibility for the explosion on senior officers on the scene and at the Pentagon, saying that not enough had been done to protect American troops from attack.

But a subsequent Air Force report, which has not been officially released, absolved Schwalier and other senior officers of any blame. It said that they did all that they could, given the information they had on possible threats.
That controversial Air Force conclusion was sent to then Defence Secretary William Perry's office last month and has not yet been released by the Pentagon.

"The delay (of Schwalier's promotion) does not in any way reflect a decision on Schwalier's promotion to major general," the Air Force said in a two-paragraph statement on Wednesday announcing the delay.
"It simply is a prudent step given that these matters are still under review" by top Pentagon leadership, it added.
Schwalier, a graduate of the Air Force Academy at Colorado Springs, is a 27-year Air Force veteran currently assigned to the service's air and space operations office at the Pentagon.
Saudi Arabia and the U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation have been jointly investigating the bombing and no culprits have been identified.
FBI and Justice Department officials said in recent days that they were not satisifed over Saudi cooperation with Washington in the investigation to date.
